attributes.description: Deity in evening air, special deity of Bráhmans, Ráma fair as Soma
Lord whose essence king bears one fourth, Ráma peer of Indra, splits mountain peak, flagstaff comparison
Lord of Fire, most glorious sphere, gave boon to Virádha that weapon/shaft may never pierce charmed frame
Death-God, grisly King when stricken worlds perishing, dark God who rules dead, Kálántaka destroyer
Lord of wealth, stern decree cursed Tumburu, angry God whose wrath fell on Tumburu for loving Rambhá
Bird deity arrows left behind, winged being
Prince, valiant hero, glorious son, splendid, fair as Soma, Indra's peer, lord and king, bravest of brave, self-ruled, exalted above heroic chiefs, Kakutstha's son
Brother, minister, Sumitrá's son, nobly brave, quick panting like spell-bound snake, Prince of men
Moonbright dame, Janak's daughter, dear to fame, Maithil dame, long in duty tried, fair of frame, wife/spouse, princess with pure glory bright, nursed in lap of soft delight
King, Sítá's father, held Maiden's Choice unparalleled, aged monarch brought to Ráma, allied with Raghu's house
Sister next to Sítá, graced with all gifts, most fair to see, given to be Lakshmana's bride
King, Ráma's sire, lost, royal power
Younger queen, cruel soul, triumphant, dark intent, expelled Ráma, greedy eyes, fatal day brings her triumph
Queen, Ráma's mother, blest to be mother of son like Ráma
Queen, Lakshmana's mother
Usurper on throne, younger queen's son, Lakshmana's fury nursed against him
Virtuous-souled matron, heard Sítá's tale, kissed lady's brow, laced loving arms, saintly dame who gave love-gifts
Saints with pitchers, fresh from bath, locks wet, bark coats dripping, tend worship fires, pure dwellers in shade
Endued with keen celestial sight, viewed chieftain with joy, came to meet prince, blessed guests, duty-loving, pure, old reverend sires bright as sun
Holy hermit, very sun is not more bright, most glorious anchorite, cot stands league beyond, blessings to earn

Giant Rákshasa, passing nature's law, vast as mountain-peak, mighty voice sunken eyes, huge hideous tall monstrous face, most ghastly of giant race, wore tiger's hide reeking with gore, carried lions/tigers/deer/wolves/elephant on iron spear, son of Java and Shatahradá, cursed Tumburu bearing hideous shape, charmed frame weapon cannot pierce, overthrown by might
Celestial minstrel, renowned among minstrel throng for song, cursed by Kuvera for loving Rambhá, wore hideous shape as Virádha, freed by Ráma's favor, spirit fled to heaven
Celestial temptress, Apsaras whose charms Tumburu loved too well, caused Kuvera's curse
Heavenly nymphs, gay dancers beneath well-loved trees
Vast shade, mighty forest, deep-tangled wood, pathless wood, wild, hermit settlement, holy dwelling, dark and drear solitude, hard rough ground

Circle where saints abode, court well-swept bright and fair, delightful grove like Brahmá's sphere, coats of bark hung, holy grass bestrewed, wild creatures refuge, birds roedeer dwelling, sheds where holy fire fed, cot with leaves overhead
O'er all sky is spread, with lunar stars engarlanded, moon risen in robes of light beautifully bright
Where monsters fierce and fell dwell, savage beasts of fearful power, pathless forests far away
Town horsemen sought, realm where hermits live
Where Virádha's spirit fled, homes eternal in skies, Brahmá's glorious sphere
Mountain summit from which rocks driven by fiery bolts
Unparalleled ceremony held by King Janak, how Ráma won Sítá's maiden hand
Sun sunk from sight, world left to holy Night, hermits return with pitchers, fires of worship tended, curling wreaths of smoke
Divine garments, ornaments, garland of celestial twine given by Anasúyá, Sítá shone like heavenly Goddess, honours high mortal dames scarce obtained
Bright with Bráhmanic lustre, holy fire fed, sacred grass and deer skins, ladles and sacrificial gear, roots fruit wood, water-urns, Veda chants, offerings burnt with fire, worldly sense subdued
One fourth of Indra's essence king bears, protector bright in fame, maintainer of right, bears awful sword, deserves elder's reverence
Fierce and fell creatures, feed on blood from human veins, assume various forms at need, savage beasts devour human flesh, rend and tear holy saints, eat them in cruel joy
Charmed frame from Brahmá's grace, weapon or shaft may never pierce or tear, rites austere long maintained
Stern decree made Tumburu wear hideous shape, when Ráma destroys thee proper shape resume and heaven give room, anger fell for loving Rambhá too well
Law ordained of old for giants when days are told, bodies laid in earth they rise to homes eternal in skies
No arms might slay charmed life, preserving life unharmed by Brahmá's saving promise, swords might rend arrows smite breast in vain, mortal arms defied
Story told of how Janak held Maiden's Choice, Ráma won hand, princes declined gift till father's mind learned, aged monarch brought, Sítá given, Urmilá to Lakshmana
Sun sunk, world left to holy Night, leafy thickets sound with birds, hermit band comes with pitchers, fires tended, smoke ascends, beasts prowl, deer reclined, night spread with lunar stars
Anasúyá bade Sítá array in heavenly raiment, shone like Goddess, love-gifts of garland ornaments robes divine, bowed to matron's feet, met lord
Ráma's heart and Lakshmana's filled with pride happiness, honored by every pious sage, sacred night hero spent well content beside darling
When night fled princes said farewell, gazed on distant shade, paid lustral rites and offerings, saints addressed warning about monsters
Ráma stood in vast shade, saw hermit settlement, bright with Bráhmanic lustre, loosed mighty bow-string, drew nearer to holy men
Mighty saints with keen celestial sight viewed chieftain with joy, came to meet prince/Sítá/Lakshmana, gave glad blessings, received in hermitage
Pure hermits led guest within cot, received with highest honor, kind observance, gave water for feet, brought stores of roots and fruit, poured blessings
Duty-loving hermits reverent hand to hand: king is protector, thou shouldst give protection, we live in thy realm, people turn to guardian
Entertained passed night, with morning's light bade adieu, pierced mighty forest where roamed deer pard bear, ruined pools scarce seen, creeper rent prostrate tree
Deep in thickets stood, saw giant passing nature's law, vast as mountain, hideous, wore tiger's hide, carried beasts on iron spear, charged with roar and yell
Fierce eye fell on three, took trembling Sítá to side, withdrew little space, demanded who are ye, threatened to make saints his meal, woman to be dame
Saw Virádha clasp Sítá, cried to brother with pale lips terror dried, Kaikeyí's blow falls, cruel soul triumphant, bitterest grief another touch Maithil dame
Ráma raised cord and arrow, seven arrows flew winged with gold, smote giant's breast, passed through bulk, fiend grasped spear wild with rage, rushed at brothers
Princely brothers poured fiery flood of arrowy rain, unmoved he stood, opened dire mouth laughed, arrows escaped from jaws, life unharmed by Brahmá's promise
Each warrior drew sword black as serpent, gathering fury rushed on giant, giant cast arm around each held heroes fast, bearing twain turned and fled
Giant upraised them to lofty shoulders, like children clung to neck, rover of night bore princes through wood vast as cloud, where birds flew trees threw shadows
Viewed with wild affright heroes hurried from sight, tossed shapely arms high, shrieked bitter cry, begged take me leave Raghu's sons free
Heroes heard mournful cry, hastened for lady's sake, Lakshmana broke foe's left arm, Ráma smashed right with heavy hand, giant came to earth fainting
Rushed on crushed and beat with arms fists feet, nerved mighty limb to pound and bray on ground, arrows and blades made wide rents, crushed torn mangled still lived could not kill
Ráma saw no arms might slay charmed life, gave counsel dig pit to fit elephantine bulk, let hollowed earth enfold giant, pressed foot upon breast

Prostrate monster heard Ráma's word with joy, addressed Kakutstha's son: I yield overthrown by might like Indra's, my name was Tumburu renowned for song, cursed by Kuvera, when Ráma destroys me proper shape assume
Tumburu freed by Ráma's favor saved to heaven go, league beyond stands holy Sharabhanga's cot, sun not more bright, quickly turn earn blessings
First under earth throw body then go rejoicing, law ordained of old for giants, bodies laid in earth rise to homes eternal in skies
Ráma dug pit to fit bulk, put foot on neck, Lakshmana plied spade dug deep wide, withdrew foot threw down mighty form, awful shout gave sank into grave, spirit fled to heaven
Princes rejoiced to see him die, strayed in boundless wood like great sun and moon triumphant in sky

Having slain Virádha, consoled spouse with gentle words, clasped in loving hold, gave counsel to brother: wild woods hard rough ground, never viewed so dark drear solitude, let us haste to Sharabhanga
